OUR COMMITMENT We are committed to demonstrating a credible account of change
through our programs.
TO ACCOUNTABILITY We undertake scheduled evaluations and reviews of all our
programs and projects to assess their impact on the lives of
participants. We focus especially on those who are the most
vulnerable or excluded, including people with disability, women
and children. Insights and lessons learned from these assessments
are used to improve the quality and effectiveness of current and
new projects and programs.
In 2024, we conducted 12 evaluations and reviews, including
seven evaluations and five mid-term reviews. Most of these
projects are supported by the Australian Government through the
Australian NGO Cooperation Program (ANCP). Our ANCP projects
are complex and often bring several sectors of community
development together. This year, substantial work took place
across five programs: climate action and natural resource
management; economic empowerment; food security, health
and nutrition; water, sanitation and hygiene; and child protection,
education and rights.

proposition: World Vision Australia developed an evidence-building strategy in 2020 aimed at improving how it collects, aggregates and uses evidence of impact.

THE WAY In 2020, we developed an evidence-building strategy aimed at improving the way we collect,
aggregate and utilise evidence of impact. This has enabled us to generate credible evidence of
our impact and effectiveness at the portfolio level. We publicly disseminate results from a series
WE MEASURE
of meta-reviews, meta-learning and case studies. For wider dissemination of our impact at scale,
we are exploring the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to translate our findings into succinct impact
statements and stories across our portfolio of projects.
IMPACT
Our evidence building and research agenda is focused on three priority evidence pillars:
climate action and regenerative environment; economic empowerment; and food security,
health and nutrition; as well as cross-cutting themes on gender equality, disability and social
inclusion.
It is implemented through our evidence building framework, involving the use of a standardised
monitoring and evaluation approach. This is to ensure a minimum level of quality assurance and
consistency in selecting a set of priority indicators for each evidence pillar. We also use a set of
guidance notes, tools and ongoing training to build capacity and support national project teams
in countries where we operate.
In 2024, we concluded three meta-reviews: Partnerships for Scaling Farmer Managed Natural
Regeneration (FMNR), FMNR Evidence Gap Map, and nutrition-sensitive agriculture.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Australian Red Cross Society has a comprehensive risk governance structure and accountability framework for managing risk, guided by a three-lines-of-engagement operating model.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Under the Australian Red Cross Society's risk governance model, the Board oversees management of risk, sets the tone from the top, and determines risk appetites and strategic risk tolerance thresholds.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Under the Australian Red Cross Society's risk governance model, the Audit & Risk Committee focuses on risk, audit assurance, and the effectiveness of controls across key risk categories.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Australian Red Cross Society's risk governance model uses first-line engagement for risk control ownership, second-line engagement for design, review and challenge, and third-line engagement for independent assurance.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Australian Red Cross Society's Executive Team is responsible for ensuring effective operationalisation of the risk management framework.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Australian Red Cross Society's risk management principles include accountability for managing risks, open and timely communication and escalation of risks, consideration of impacts on quality, client and community outcomes, stakeholder confidence and trust, and organisational sustainability, and learning from mistakes and successes.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Lifeblood operates four main processing and testing facilities and a network of collection centres in metropolitan and regional areas across Australia.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society had 18,355 members and volunteers supporting fundraising and advocacy efforts.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The financial report covers Australian Red Cross Society as an individual entity.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society is formed and domiciled in Australia.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society is a not-for-profit private-sector organisation for the purpose of preparing its financial statements.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society’s financial statements are prepared by combining the financial statements of its Humanitarian Services and Lifeblood divisions.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society eliminates all balances and transactions between its Humanitarian Services and Lifeblood divisions, as well as unrealised profits arising within the entity, in full when preparing its financial statements.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society is a signatory to the Australian Council for International Development Code of Conduct and is committed to full adherence to its requirements.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society’s financial statements are presented in Australian dollars, which is its functional and presentation currency.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society reported total assets of $973.444 million as at 30 June 2024.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society reported total liabilities of $606.774 million as at 30 June 2024.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society reported net assets of $366.670 million as at 30 June 2024.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society reported total equity of $366.670 million as at 30 June 2024.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society reported a net deficit of $51.346 million for the year ended 30 June 2024.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society generated net cash of $38.042 million from operating activities for the year ended 30 June 2024.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: Australian Red Cross Society had cash and cash equivalents of $235.835 million at the end of the financial year ended 30 June 2024.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society receives part of its income from cash or in-kind donations.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society does not recognise pledged donations as revenue until cash is received because it does not have an enforceable right to require donors to meet their pledges.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society recognises bequests at the fair value of the benefit received when receipt is virtually certain by grant of probate.
qualifications: Where required, bequests are recognised in accordance with the express terms of the will under AASB 1058.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society recognises sponsorship revenue at a point in time under AASB 15 when the performance obligation has been met.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society does not recognise volunteer services in its financial statements because their fair value is not reliably measurable in financial terms.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society is exempt from income tax under subsection 50-5 of the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.
qualifications: The financial statements describe the Society as a public benevolent institution.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society is registered as a deductible gift recipient for tax purposes.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society recognises loss allowances for expected credit losses on specified financial assets, including investments in debt instruments measured at amortised cost or FVOCI, lease receivables, trade receivables and contract assets.
qualifications: The allowance is updated at each reporting date to reflect changes in credit risk since initial recognition.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society always recognises lifetime expected credit losses for trade receivables, contract assets and lease receivables.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society recognises lifetime expected credit losses for other financial instruments when credit risk has increased significantly since initial recognition; otherwise, it measures the loss allowance at 12-month expected credit losses.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society normally settles trade and other receivables within 30 days.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society subsequently measures trade and other receivables at amortised cost.
qualifications: This is consistent with the Society’s business model for managing financial assets and the contractual cash-flow characteristics of the assets.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society generally settles trade and other payables within 30 days of recognition.
qualifications: The payables are unsecured.

proposition: The Society recognises payments for leases of 12 months or less and leases of low-value assets as an expense on a straight-line basis over the lease term when no lease asset and lease liability are recognised.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society accounts for subleases classified as operating leases by recognising rental income on a straight-line basis over the lease term.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society contributes to staff retirement funds comprising both defined benefit and accumulation schemes.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The defined benefit funds operated by the Society are ActiveSuper in New South Wales and the Australian Red Cross Queensland Staff Retirement Fund.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society recognises contributions to defined contribution retirement benefit plans as an expense when employees have rendered service entitling them to the contributions.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society determines the cost of providing defined benefit retirement plans using the projected unit credit method, with actuarial valuations at the end of each annual reporting period.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Society discounts its defined benefit obligations and other long-term employee benefits using the high-quality corporate bond rate published by the Group of 100.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Australian Red Cross Society comprises two operating divisions: Australian Red Cross Humanitarian Services and Australian Red Cross Lifeblood.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: For the year ended 30 June 2024, the Australian Red Cross Society reported total revenue of $1,090.174 million, total expenditure of $1,141.520 million, and a net deficit of $51.346 million.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: For the year ended 30 June 2024, the Australian Red Cross Society reported total comprehensive deficit of $47.324 million.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: For the year ended 30 June 2024, the Australian Red Cross Society reported total government funding of $914.531 million, comprising $785.521 million in Commonwealth operating funding, $70.691 million in State operating funding, and $58.319 million in Commonwealth and State capital funding.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: For the year ended 30 June 2024, the Australian Red Cross Society reported donations, bequests and sponsorships of $79.161 million, rendering of services of $7.802 million, sale of goods of $39.005 million, non-government grants of $13.829 million, investment revenue of $16.247 million, and other income of $19.599 million.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Australian Red Cross Society identified employees eligible for portable long-service benefits in Queensland, Victoria and the Australian Capital Territory and pays levies to the respective authorities of 1.35%, 1.65% and 1.6% of eligible employees’ wages, respectively.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Australian Red Cross Society applied all new and revised Australian Accounting Standards applicable for the first time at 30 June 2024, including AASB 2021-2 and AASB 2021-6.

subject: Australian Red Cross Society
proposition: The Australian Red Cross Society decided not to early adopt new and amended accounting standards and interpretations issued but not yet effective at 30 June 2024.

Responsibilities of the Board Members for the Financial Report
The Board Members of the Society are responsible for the preparation of the financial report that gives a true and
fair view in accordance with Australian Accounting Standards and the ACNC Act and the ACFID code of conduct
and for such internal control as the Board Members determine is necessary to enable the preparation of the

conditions that may cast significant doubt on the Society’s ability to continue as a going concern. If we
conclude that a material uncertainty exists, we are required to draw attention in our auditor’s report to
the related disclosures in the financial report or, if such disclosures are inadequate, to modify our
opinion. Our conclusions are based on the audit evidence obtained up to the date of our auditor’s report.
